speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin, have you experienced any shortness of breath, sweating, or pain radiating to your arm or jaw?

REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
REQUEST TEST: Serum Troponin

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ECG and troponin results are normal, which helps rule out an acute heart attack, but your symptoms remain concerning. Have you noticed any specific triggers for your vomiting, such as eating fatty foods, or have you experienced severe abdominal pain, fever, or bloating?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Complete Metabolic Panel

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal ECG and troponin levels rule out a heart attack, but we still need to investigate your abdomen. Have you noticed any abdominal pain, bloating, or changes in your bowel habits?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Complete Metabolic Panel

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your ECG, troponin, and initial abdominal ultrasound are normal, have you noticed any specific triggers for your vomiting, such as eating fatty or spicy foods, or do you experience severe pain radiating to your back?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound (Pancreas focus)
REQUEST TEST: Lipase

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal lipase and focused ultrasound have ruled out acute pancreatitis and other common abdominal emergencies. Given your persistent vomiting and chest pain with a completely normal cardiac workup and abdominal imaging, have you recently undergone any general anesthesia, neck surgery, or experienced a head injury?

REQUEST TEST: Head CT
REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Endoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal head CT and upper GI endoscopy effectively rule out increased intracranial pressure and upper gastrointestinal pathology, which explains your persistent vomiting and chest pain.

Since we have exhausted cardiac, abdominal, and neurological causes, I need to ask: Do you experience severe pain that worsens when you lie down and improves when you sit up, and have you noticed any coughing up blood or significant shortness of breath?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal chest X-ray and arterial blood gas effectively rule out pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, and acidosis. With cardiac, abdominal, neurological, and respiratory causes excluded, do you experience a sensation of fullness or bloating in your esophagus, or do you have a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)?

REQUEST TEST: Barium Swallow
REQUEST TEST: 24-Hour pH Monitoring

speaker: Doctor
text:
I am sorry to report that the Barium Swallow and 24-hour pH monitoring results are also normal, which is unusual given your persistent symptoms. Since we have systematically ruled out cardiac, abdominal, neurological, pulmonary, and typical esophageal causes, does your chest pain feel like a sharp, stabbing sensation, and have you noticed any pain worsening with deep inspiration or movement?

REQUEST TEST: Stress Test (Pharmacological)
REQUEST TEST: Esophageal Manometry

speaker: Doctor
text:
We have now exhausted the standard diagnostic workup for cardiac, abdominal, neurological, pulmonary, and typical esophageal causes, all of which have returned normal results. Given your persistent vomiting and chest pain that remains unexplained by these common conditions, do you experience pain or pressure specifically when swallowing, or do you have a history of eating disorders like bulimia?

REQUEST TEST: Esophageal Manometry (repeat with high sensitivity)
REQUEST TEST: Contrast Esophagram

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Factitious Disorder Imposed on Self (Munchausen Syndrome). The patient has presented with persistent vomiting and chest pain, yet every requested diagnostic test (ECG, troponin, CT, Endoscopy, Manometry, etc.) has returned normal results, indicating the symptoms are not caused by an underlying organic disease. This pattern of chronic, unexplained symptoms coupled with a consistent history of normal medical testing despite severe complaints is highly characteristic of factitious disorder.
